resources.string: nothing yet for the previous days

This app reads, on the phone itself, which apps came to the front and when. From that it counts the openings of the apps you open by reflex, social networks, games, short video, and tells them from the ones you use as tools. Nothing leaves the phone, and nothing is blocked.
the system page where this app is given “usage access”
a pause before a reflex app

When a reflex app comes to the front: its name, today’s count, and a question. Light: a reason to tap, then “go on” after six seconds. Firm: the reason typed in a few words, and twelve seconds. Breathing: five breaths guided by a ring, about a minute, then the question. Longer in the evening. You can always go on. From an app’s row on the first page, the pause can be set for that app alone. Needs the accessibility service below.
One line at the top of the screen, for a few seconds, when a reflex app has stayed in front that long. Needs the accessibility service below.
After this hour the pause lasts longer, and the evening’s reflex minutes are counted on the first page.
The service hears only which app comes to the front. It reads nothing on the screen and performs no gesture.

Reader\'s Attention watches only which app comes to the front, to offer a pause before a reflex app and a word after a while. It reads nothing on the screen, performs no gesture, and nothing leaves the phone.

resources.string: A notification that arrives between two delivery times waits, then they all come at once. Three times a day is enough to miss nothing and few enough to stop looking. Calls, alarms, reminders, navigation, what is in progress, and the apps marked below always come at once. Nothing is blocked, only delivered later; what is already waiting still comes at its time. Needs notification access below.
A notification that arrives between two of these times waits for the next one. A tap changes or removes a time.
The apps whose notifications never wait, whatever the time. The marked ones come first; a tap marks or unmarks.

The system page where this app is allowed to see notifications, so it can hold them until the next delivery time. It looks only at the app and the kind of each one, reads no content, and removes none.
